name: Chest-supported row
cue: Keep your chest on the pad and drive your elbows back.
research: research.json biomech.chest_row: seated, sternum on a chest pad tilted with the 10 deg forward lean (pad top just below shoulder level), hips ~100, knees 90, feet flat. Neutral grip on vertical handles just outside the pad. Start: shoulder flexion 85, elbows ~9 deg out of the sagittal plane, elbow ~10, shoulder blades spread (clav pro +20); end: shoulder extension 35, abduction 25, elbow 125, shoulder blades squeezed (clav pro -20, elev -5), forearm in line with the pull. Hands start ~61 cm in front of and ~9 cm below the shoulders and finish beside the lower ribs ~23 cm below them. Each vertical handle hangs from a pin 0.05 H above the grip centre on a lever pivoting above and in front of the lifter (pin radius 0.475 H = 0.85 m, 40.6 deg of swing; tools/design/chest_row.mjs) and swivels about the lateral axis (dof swivel, stored per key), so it always lies along the fist tunnel of a neutral wrist: wrist flexion stays within -2.4..1.6 deg (a handle fixed to the lever swung the wrist 15 deg palmar -> 12 deg dorsal). Via keys at 25/50/75 % put the FK pin on the lever arc with the elbow flare interpolated 7 -> 21 deg, so the elbows stay tucked through the pull. The skin is bound 0.3 s into the pull (motion.bind { phase: con, at: 0.296 }: early in the pull, arms still reaching forward): at the default mid-pull bind the upper arms hang beside the flanks, the lateral edge of the lat patch snaps onto the arm and lat glow was painted down the humerus (a speck beside the far elbow at the peak). Bound there, the lat glow ends at its insertion, at most 0.054 H below the humeral head, like the lat pulldown. Muscles: lats, mid traps and upper back (rhomboids, teres, infraspinatus), the research primaries. The trap_mid and upper_back footprints were re-cut (tools/muscles_src.mjs) so they meet along the scapular spine without a dark bay and leave a clean midline edge at the peak. v10 (science audit A12, optional): the elbows finish ~45 deg out (v9 21; Jeff 2026: ~45 deg to bias the upper back since the pulldown covers the lats; anatomy only, no trial). tools/design/chest_row_v10.mjs: the start is the v9 start; the finish is fitted to the flare, the grip x, height and depth; hand pro (forearm rotation) is keyed (90 at the reach, ~55 at the finish) so the upright swivel handle stays on the fist tunnel as the arm turns in; via keys put the FK pin on the lever arc with the flare opening from 8 to 45. The hands travel from x 0.128 to 0.164 H, so the lever pivot sits at x 0.1359.

targets.note: v10 (science audit A12): the elbows finish ~45 deg out of the sagittal plane (Jeff 2026: ~45 deg bias the upper back; v9 21) after opening from 8 at the reach; shoulder extension 46 at the finish. Wrist held to +-8 deg (research: neutral wrist); the swivel handle keeps it within a few degrees, the forearm turning (hand pro keyed) so the handle stays upright as the humerus rotates in.

camera.note: Research view is az 110 / el 10 (side, a little behind); the research best_camera asks for a three-quarter rear view about 45 deg between the side and the back. Turned 30 deg further behind (az 140) and raised 5 deg (el 15): the lats, mid traps and upper back read as one shape either side of the spine and the shoulder blades visibly squeeze, while the elbows driving back past the ribs still read along the near arm. The brightest bare skin is the rim on the front of the near shoulder, so do not lower the camera. The machine stands on a floor rail from the seat post to the column, the column foot and a foot plate under the feet (a plate under everything ran under the exercise name on the phone).
